question: Braess's classic 4,000-driver network: two routes take 65 minutes each. A free link is added and drivers choose selfishly. New trip time in minutes?
move: Adding an option can hurt everyone when each chooses only for themselves.
trap: Under 65, since a free road can only help.
hint: Each route has a variable road taking cars/100 minutes and a fixed road taking 45; the link joins the variable roads.
steps: Before: 2,000 cars per variable road, so 20 + 45 = 65 minutes.
With the link, any driver on a fixed road switches: 40 or less beats 45.
If all 4,000 use both variable roads, each takes 4,000 / 100 = 40 minutes.
reference: Braess, Über ein Paradoxon aus der Verkehrsplanung, Unternehmensforschung, 1968
